comparison: Perfect agreement on immune subtyping validation (C77-C78). Both evaluations find this analysis provides independent validation of immune down-regulation findings and support the conclusions without challenge.

Strong agreement on methodological rigor (C14-C20). OpenEval notes the approach is 'methodologically sound' with justified statistical methods, while peer reviewers praised 'solid comparative analysis' and 'rigorous' methods. Both also address predictive performance (C23-C24), with OpenEval noting modest improvement and peer reviewers highlighting stronger predictive power of Boruta-selected genes.

Strong agreement on GO enrichment analysis (C32-C39, C90-C91). Both find the analysis thorough and identify interesting findings in DNA damage processes. OpenEval cautions about causal language in C39, while peer reviewers accepted the interpretation without challenge. Both support the robustness analysis.

Strong agreement on high-confidence candidate genes (C92-C98). Both accept the ranking methodology and the key observation that CorEx genes are not themselves on ecDNA (C93-C94). OpenEval notes therapeutic claims (C98) require validation, while peer reviewers accepted the distinction between ecDNA-encoded and chromosomal genes. Peer review also covers down-regulated genes (C99-C101).

Strong agreement on immune pathway down-regulation (C59-C71). OpenEval documents comprehensive down-regulation with appropriate statistics but notes bulk RNA-seq limitations. Peer reviewers highlighted this as having 'important theoretical implications' for treatment. Peer review also covers cancer immune cycle mapping (C72-C76) and summary claims (C102-C103, C107-C109) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Strong agreement on DSB repair pathway analysis (C40-C48). Both find detailed pathway analysis well-documented with appropriate statistics. OpenEval cautions that expression data alone cannot prove functional pathway preference, while peer reviewers accepted the mechanistic interpretation as consistent with prior observations of microhomologies. Peer review also covers gene-level analysis (C49-C58) and mechanistic interpretation (C106) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on gene-level DSB repair analysis (C49-C58). OpenEval finds the pattern consistent with alternative pathway usage but notes expression alone doesn't prove functional preference. Peer reviewers accepted the DNA damage findings as 'interesting' without challenging the interpretation. Peer review R4 also covers broader pathway claims (C40-C48, C106) that OpenEval addresses in R9.

Agreement on cancer immune cycle mapping (C72-C76). OpenEval finds the framework application appropriate with good statistical support but cautions about bulk RNA-seq limitations. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the broader immune down-regulation story without specific challenge. Peer review R5 also covers broader immune claims (C59-C71, C102-C103, C107-C109) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on CorEx gene characterization (C29-C31). OpenEval notes modest effect sizes suggest subtle but consistent changes. Peer reviewers accepted these as persistent transcriptional differences. Peer review R2 also covers pan-cancer validation (C21, C25-C28) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on cross-tumor-type validation (C25-C28). OpenEval finds appropriate statistical testing with sarcoma exception explained, but cautions about causal inference in C28. Peer reviewers noted authors 'addressed all comments satisfactorily' and accepted the sarcoma contextualization. Peer review R2 also covers tumor purity (C21) and CorEx characterization (C29-C31) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on tumor purity difference (C21). OpenEval notes this is statistically significant but could introduce bias requiring careful interpretation. Peer reviewers accepted the authors' supplementary analyses addressing this concern. Peer review R2 also covers broader pan-cancer findings (C25-C31) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on mutation burden analysis (C79-C81). Both accept this important negative result showing the pan-cancer difference is driven by tumor type composition rather than ecDNA status per se. Peer review R6 also covers specific gene mutations (C82-C84, C87-C89) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on differentially mutated genes (C82-C84). OpenEval finds TP53 robust and biologically plausible but notes causal interpretation requires validation. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as consistent with previous work. Peer review R6 also covers mutation burden (C79-C81) and signature analysis (C87-C89) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on mutation signature analysis (C87-C89). Both accept the APOBEC signature finding as validation of prior work and the negative result that mutations are less informative than expression for ecDNA prediction. Peer review R6 also covers mutation burden (C79-C81) and specific genes (C82-C84) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on predictive performance (C23-C24). OpenEval notes modest but statistically significant improvement with overall low AUPRC values indicating prediction remains challenging. Peer reviewers highlighted that Boruta-selected genes have 'stronger predictive power' than top log-fold change genes. Peer review R1 primarily focuses on methodology (C14-C20) that OpenEval addresses in R3.

Agreement on robustness analysis (C90-C91). OpenEval finds this sensitivity analysis strengthens confidence in biological conclusions. Peer reviewers did not specifically critique this but accepted the GO enrichment findings as thorough. Peer review R3 primarily focuses on GO analysis (C32-C39) that OpenEval addresses in R8.

Agreement on persistent down-regulated genes (C99-C101). OpenEval notes literature support for tumor suppressor roles but unclear functional significance. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without challenge as part of the candidate gene analysis. Peer review R7 primarily focuses on up-regulated genes (C92-C98) that OpenEval addresses in R18.

Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval (C107-C110) finds expression data well-supported but STING agonist therapeutic suggestion (C110) speculative and not directly tested. Peer reviewers similarly note the therapeutic suggestion is speculative, with biological interpretation remaining 'observational' and lacking experimental validation.

Partial overlap on immune findings (C107-C109). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by expression data but cautions about mechanistic interpretation. Peer review R5 covers these as part of broader immune down-regulation (C59-C76, C102-C103) which they find has important theoretical implications. OpenEval addresses therapeutic speculation (C110) separately.

Divergent evaluations on conclusions. OpenEval finds summary claims (C102-C106) SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about therapeutic implications and mechanistic inferences requiring validation. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that interpretations remain 'observational' and 'would be more robust with experimental validation.' Similar concerns about concluding claims (C114-C115).

Divergent evaluations on concluding interpretation. OpenEval finds claims (C114-C115) SUPPORTED as appropriate contextualization, though notes causal language about 'contributing to formation and pathogenesis' goes beyond correlation data. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic claims about causality and therapeutic targeting require experimental validation.

Minor overlap on summary claims (C102-C103). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as appropriate summary of main findings. Peer review R5 accepts these findings as having 'important theoretical implications' but peer review R10 notes broader interpretations remain observational. Peer review R5 primarily focuses on immune findings (C59-C76, C107-C109).

Minimal overlap on mechanistic interpretation (C106). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with caveat that mechanistic inferences require validation. Peer review R4 accepts DNA damage findings but peer review R10 notes broader mechanistic claims remain observational. Peer review R4 primarily focuses on DSB repair pathways (C40-C58).

OpenEval evaluates background/literature claims (C1-C8) as SUPPORTED by citations to prior published work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are standard background claims not typically scrutinized in peer review.

OpenEval evaluates sample selection methodology (C9-C12) as SUPPORTED with clear rationale, noting potential selection bias. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing sample selection criteria.

OpenEval evaluates literature contextualization claims (C111-C113) as SUPPORTED citations to prior work on TMB and immunotherapy response. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are citations rather than novel findings.
